newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bolivia, Chile may not be in Brazil-Mercosur deal.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia, Chile may not be in Brazil-Mercosur deal.

text.p: Confusion reigned on Thursday in the Brazilian capital as to whether Mercosur free trade associates Bolivia and Chile were included in a deal on import finance rules struck between Brasilia and the trade bloc.

Jose Botafogo Goncalves, general sub-secretary of economic integration and foreign trade at Brazil's Foreign Ministry, said he was unaware the deal had been stretched to include Chile and Bolivia, contradicting earlier comments from the Central Bank.
"I am unaware of any change (in the original decision)," Botafogo told reporters. "Mercosur consists of four countries. Chile and Bolivia are associated to it."

Earlier, Central Bank Director of International Affairs Gustavo Franco said partial exemptions from new Brazilian limits on short-term import financing granted to some Mercosur products were also valid for Chile and Bolivia.
That interpretation made its way to Santiago, where President Eduardo Frei said Chile would be treated the same as full Mercosur members Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

But in a decree setting up the Mercosur exemptions, which was due to be published on Friday, the Central Bank limited the new conditions to "members of Mercosur", which Botafogo said clearly referred to the four full members only.
He said Chilean officials would travel to Brasilia to discuss the matter, as originally announced by Finance Minister Pedro Malan on Wednesday.
Frei said in Santiago that Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia would go to Brasilia Thursday.

In the deal struck Wednesday, Brazil agreed to make its limits on import financing of less than 360 days more flexible for Mercosur products. Imports worth less than $40,000 are exempt and the definition of what constitutes paying in cash was lengthened to 89 days from 59 days.
